newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on Argentine wheat talk.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on Argentine wheat talk.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower on talk Argentine wheat prices dropped on improved weather prospects in that country's wheat growing region, traders said.
"There was talk Argentine wheat prices broke four or five dollars (per tonne)," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
A wheat rally early this week was partly due to concern about rain damage to the Argentine crop and to talk Argentina raised its wheat prices.
Futures also closed lower on diminished fears about cold weather damage to the U.S. winter wheat crop.
"Argentina is drying out so that hurt wheat (prices) plus there is snow coming this weekend in Kansas which may help the crop," a trader said.
Weather Services Corp Peter Leavitt Friday said some snow could fall in the far northern Midwest this weekend.

The market was underpinned by recent imports of wheat by India and news Iraq was buying wheat on the world market. Also Pakistan is slated in the market over the weekend and there was talk Tunisia soon will be in the market.
Wheat closed 3-3/4 to seven cents per bushel lower, with March down seven at $3.93-1/4 a bushel.

Strong commercial stopping of the deliveries posted Friday against the expired December contract also underpinned prices, the traders said. Term Commodities, the marketing arm for Louis Dreyfus Corp, stopped all of the 890,000 bushels posted Friday for delivery on the December, according to the CBOT.
Refco Inc bought two million bushels of March and bought 1.5 million July, traders said. Rand Financial sold two million bushels of July, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 10,000 contracts, below the 15,756 traded Thursday, according to the CBOT.
Farmers Commodities Corp sold 125 July $3.50 calls at 17 to 17-1/2 cents, Tenco Inc bought 100 May $3.70 calls at 19 cents and bought 100 July $3.50 calls at 17 to 18 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 4,000 contracts, below the 5,630 traded Thursday.
